title_as_printed: Solubility of CO2 by analysis of the liquid phase
pressure_note: pc = partial pressure of CO2 (atm): total vessel pressure measured just before sampling minus the saturated water vapour pressure of water (Dorsey 1940) or of the NaCl solution (Raoult's-law corrected); above 300 C a further ~1 percent Raoult correction for dissolved CO2 was applied (text p. 50).

value.what: moles CO2 per mole H2O in the liquid phase, from weighed CO2 (Carbosorb) and water/salt solution in a ~2 g liquid sample; printed x10^3

fugacity_coefficient.what: fugacity coefficient of CO2 from Majumdar and Roy (1956)

henry.what: Henry's law coefficient K = fc/x = pc*alpha/x, x = nCO2/(nCO2+nH2O) in the solution; printed x10^-3

z.what: compressibility factor of pure CO2 at T and pc, from graphs of Sweigert, Weber and Allen (1946)

ostwald.what: Ostwald coefficient = g CO2/cc liquid / g CO2/cc vapour, using the Table 1 solution densities and pure-CO2 vapour density

composition.other_species: none (water and NaCl solutions; molal = moles of salt per 1000 g water, text p. 47)

conversion_needs: value x 1e-3 = mol CO2 per mol H2O (salt-free ratio); to mol/kg water multiply by 1000/18.015
pc atm -> MPa x 0.101325; pc is a CO2 partial pressure, total pressure = pc + water (or brine) vapour pressure, not printed
notes: Table spans p. 52 (Water, 0.5m, 1 m NaCl) and p. 53 (Table 2 continued, 2 m NaCl); blocks written in printed order. Water block NaCl = 0 set by group row. Replicate rows at the same T are separate samples at different pc.
